intro: Every day a pair of dice rolls a pile of unrelated words, and the game has to use all of them. Today: a closed umbrella who lost a bet, trading, marbles, fame, paperwork, gamelan, pirate radio, paper cutouts. Here is how they ended up in one cupboard. Today's roll was seed 643226831.

rolls.value: a closed umbrella who lost a bet
rolls.became: Gamp, a chatty umbrella who has lived in the school's Lost Property cupboard for six years. It bet the Recorder that it was the most famous thing in there and that someone would claim it by Friday. Nobody did. The forfeit: keep shut (an umbrella talks by flapping open) until the whole school knows its name. That rose-pink strap round its middle is the forfeit.

Radio Rummage. The forfeit said nothing about radio, a shut umbrella is exactly the shape of an aerial, and Lost Property has a transistor nobody claimed. Gamp plugs its tip in, and goes on air without ever opening its mouth.

Lost Property's biggest stock, by a mile. Kids find marbles everywhere (behind the climbing frame, under the benches, in the bike shed) and post them through the Lost Property hatch, because that is where found things go. Nobody ever comes back for a marble.

It's a swap shop, the oldest format in radio. Three clearies for a cat's eye, three cat's eyes for a swirl, three swirls for a steelie, live on air with whoever's calling in. Every swap read out wins listeners.
Everything posted in drops onto the mat, and Gamp reads out each marble as it goes into its own jar: clearies, cat's eyes, swirls, steelies. Drag them in by hand to start with.

rolls.value: a production chain on a small belt grid you lay out
rolls.became: The cloakroom floor is five squares by four. Lay rulers to push marbles sideways, comb gates to let one kind fall through and nudge the rest along, and swap desks (pencil cases on their sides) that turn three of a kind into one better marble. A staircase of desks turns a pile of clearies into steelies.
The forfeit ends when the whole school knows Gamp's name: 360 pupils, all listening at once. The record meter is the bet.
Everything counts in hundreds: 360 pupils, a few hundred marbles per jar, a couple of hundred Claim Forms.

Mrs. Pettigrew, the school secretary, runs Lost Property, and nothing leaves it without a signed Claim Form. Every swap sends three marbles out, so every swap makes a form, and they fly off to her In Tray. She stamps them one at a time. If the tray fills up, she suspends all swaps until she's caught up. Gamp can help by falling on the forms.

rolls.value: you pay with something you need
rolls.became: Gamp can't build and broadcast at the same time. Every piece and upgrade costs listeners: dead air, and they wander off. The very thing that wins the bet (and makes kids post in more marbles) is the money. The record never drops, though.

rolls.value: an ending you have to be talked out of
rolls.became: When the whole school is listening, the forfeit is over and a kid comes to the hatch to take the famous umbrella home. Gamp undoes its strap to open up and go. You press the button. Three times, somebody talks it out of it: Mrs. Pettigrew with a form, the whole playground, and the Recorder.

The Recorder says Gamp is the only one who ever played it (that was the Play the Recorder upgrade). Then every lost thing in the cupboard wants on air too: the PE shorts do the weather, the welly does sport, Mrs. Pettigrew stamps forms live. A shut umbrella is an aerial, and the station needs one. Gamp keeps shut.
About twenty to thirty minutes: sorting by hand, laying out the floor, swirls at 60 listeners and steelies at 150, then the whole school.
Everything is cut out of construction paper, with slightly wobbly scissor edges and a hard shadow, including the title, done as a ransom note (it is a pirate station).
Its sixteen colours do everything: plum for the cupboard, mint and teal for clearies and cat's eyes, pink for swirls, slate for steelies, rose for Gamp's strap.

A soft cut-paper gamelan in D minor pentatonic: a gong closing every cycle, a metallophone skeleton melody, a bonang filling in between and a kendhang drum. It speeds up as the station takes off. Every plink, swap and stamp is on the same five notes. Buy Play the Recorder and the Recorder joins the music.
Gamp's patter: shout-outs to Jordan in 3B, station idents from under the coats, and apologies for the dead air.
No calendar nod today. Just a cupboard, a bet and a lot of marbles.

outro: Nobody chose any of this. The dice did. We just took it seriously.
